findings.can_model_run_cpu_only: Partially YES. The .trt TensorRT engines CANNOT run on CPU at all (TensorRT requires an NVIDIA GPU). However Cell 2 ships a complete ONNX Runtime fallback path that explicitly supports CPUExecutionProvider, and the fp32 2x ONNX model exists (Dropbox link). So CPU-only inference is technically possible via onnxruntime + the ONNX weight only (2x, FP32).
findings.encoders_blocker: Cell 2's x264/x265 paths use h264_nvenc / hevc_nvenc - NVIDIA hardware encoders that hard-fail on a CPU-only runner. ProRes (prores_ks) and FFV1 are CPU encoders and would work. A GitHub Actions version would need the encoder mapped to libx264/libx265 (or ProRes/FFV1) - a small code change but mandatory.
findings.runner_limits: GitHub-hosted Linux runner: 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, ~14 GB SSD, 6-hour max job runtime, 2 GB artifact/file limits on releases. The 24-channel tiled CNN at 576x672 tiles on 4 CPU cores would plausibly take tens of seconds to minutes PER FRAME - a 10s 24fps clip (240 frames, 3 first-frame passes + temporal) could exceed the 6h job limit. Input must also be tiny (1080p pre-resize helps but 2x output of 1080p = 4K frames in RAM).
findings.feasibility_verdict: Technically feasible for very short/small test clips (proof-of-pipeline), NOT practical for real videos. Complexity: moderate (rewrite setup cell for CPU-only pip, swap NVENC->libx264/libx265, download ONNX from the Release, upload result as workflow artifact). Recommendation: keep Colab GPU as the product; Actions version only as a demo/smoke-test.
